data.title: The Bedroom

thumbnail.alt_text: Painting of bedroom, blue walls, green window, tan bed, red bedding.

data.short_description: In 1888, Van Gogh moved into his own home in Arles, France. He dubbed it the “Studio of the South,” hoping that fellow artists would join him there to work. This is one of three versions he painted of his beloved Arles bedroom. While its vivid palette and dramatic perspective seem to burst with nervous vitality, Van Gogh intended the painting "to express utter repose."

data.title: Paris Street; Rainy Day

thumbnail.alt_text: Life-size painting of an urban scene in Paris. A man in a top hat holding an umbrella and a woman in a long fashionable dark dress walk arm in arm toward the viewer as other city dwellers with umbrellas walk in various directions across cobblestone roads and sidewalks.

data.short_description: Considered Caillebotte’s masterpiece, this view of a busy intersection captures both an everyday moment and all that was new in a rapidly changing Paris. The clothes are the latest fashion. The retractable umbrella was just invented. And a decades-long renovation had transformed the medieval streets of Paris into grand boulevards, like the ones seen here. It's a painting you want to walk into.

data.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884

thumbnail.alt_text: Large painting of people in a crowded park, brushstrokes are dots.

data.short_description: For his largest and best-known painting, Georges Seurat depicted Parisians enjoying all sorts of leisurely activities—strolling, lounging, sailing, and fishing—in the park called La Grande Jatte on the River Seine. He used an innovative technique called Pointillism that was inspired by optical and color theory, applying tiny dabs of different colored paint that viewers would see as a single, and Seurat believed, more brilliant hue.

data.title: The Assumption of the Virgin

thumbnail.alt_text: Painting of the Virgin Mary ascending to heaven amongst multitude of angels.

data.artist_display: El Greco (Doménikos Theotokópoulos; Greek, active in Spain, 1541–1614)
data.short_description: This painting was the central element of an altarpiece that was El Greco’s ﬁrst major Spanish commission and large public work. The Virgin ﬂoats upward on the crescent moon, a symbol of her purity, while the apostles express amazement and concern. El Greco’s broad brushstrokes and bold color made this painting a favorite of modern artists such as Pablo Picasso and Mary Cassatt.
